notes: 3 of 13 flagged items (relationships[11], relationships[13], relationships[23]) all shared the same defect: an evidence/rationale text naming or paraphrasing a real, citable source class/predicate that wasn't in the mapping's own source_iris -- the same category rounds 3-4 were meant to have eliminated. relationships[13] had actually already been 'fixed' once in round 4 (for a different, unrelated citation gap on the same item) -- its round-4 reground rewrite introduced fresh prose that itself named TemperatureSetpoint without citing it, and nothing rescanned the fix's own output afterward.

User directed escalation ('yes, escalate and fix the normalization gap for all 3'). Investigation found the round-3/4 scan's label-matching never accounted for evidence text using the domain's own compiled PascalCase class name (e.g. 'TemperatureDeadbandSetpoint') instead of the source ontology's spaced label ('Temperature Deadband Setpoint') -- a third distinct scan-methodology gap, after case-sensitivity (round 4) and short-label filtering (round 4).

Comprehensive rescan (all 127 mappings, not just the sample) with a corrected matcher: word-boundary case-insensitive matching PLUS a second check for the label's no-space form appearing as an exact contiguous alphabetic token in the evidence text (catching compiled-name mentions without the substring-collision false positives a naive no-space substring search produces, e.g. 'Wing' inside 'flowing'). Raw hits filtered by an expanded stoplist (generic English words that double as real but non-specific Brick/REC labels: area, regulates, capacity, includes, plus the round-4 stoplist) and by a synonym-cluster check (AHU/Air_Handler_Unit/Air_Handling_Unit; Brick/REC area; Brick/REC Occupancy_Sensor/OccupancySensorEquipment; Heat_Exchanger/HX -- citing any one member of a real synonym cluster already covers a mention of another member, not a fresh gap). Every remaining candidate manually read against its actual relationship endpoints (from reference.domain.yaml) to separate genuine uncited endpoints from incidental mentions inside an already-cited class's own quoted definition (e.g. 'Fan' appearing only because it's part of AirHandlingUnit's own quoted definition, not because this specific mapping is about Fan) or self-critical caveat text (a rationale explicitly disclaiming a claim isn't well-grounded is not a citation gap).

Result: 21 genuine items, dominated by AirHandlingUnit-family relationships (hasPart/hasPoint/feeds) whose 'from' or 'to' endpoint was named in evidence prose but never cited in that same mapping's source_iris, plus a few predicate citations (hasPart, feeds) that were described in prose but never formally cited. relationships[29] is now a third-round finding on the same target_path (flagged in round 3's raw scan, never made the final 42; still uncited after round 4's fix pass touched a different item) -- worth noting as a reminder that 'no longer flagged' isn't the same guarantee as 'genuinely fixed' until a rescan with the corrected matcher actually re-clears it.

Root-cause fix, not just a data patch: repair.py's apply_repairs() now unions old and new source_iris for reground decisions instead of replacing wholesale (the same defect class found in round 4, now also confirmed to have independently caused relationships[23]'s hasPart citation to be dropped during round 3's own fix, and to partly explain why round 3's own scan-flagged 'Space' endpoint for relationships[23] was silently dropped from that batch's construction and never applied). New regression test: tests/test_repair.py::test_reground_merges_source_iris_instead_of_replacing.

Fix applied directly (pure Python source_iris addition, no LLM repair call needed -- the evidence/rationale prose already correctly named every concept added; only the citation itself was missing, unlike rounds 3-4's fixes which also needed the prose rewritten).

sampling_method.description: Stratified sample by artefact type, proportional allocation, new seed. Escalated mid-round, per explicit direction, to a full non-sampled audit of all 127 mappings plus all 12 competency questions.

notes: 12 of 13 sampled items clean, including confirmation that all four round-5 fixes held (relationships[2], relationships[29] -- a third-round recurring miss, finally resolved -- relationships[32], actions.maintainWithinDeadband).

1 flagged: classes.TemperatureSensor.properties.value paraphrased Temperature_Sensor's own real definition ('temperature sensor definition says it measures temperature') without citing it -- the same defect family as rounds 3-5, but this time on a fresh item never touched before.

User directed: 'do an utterly complete check. Basically everything. the whole ontology. all rules. EVERYTHING. Give me only the flagged problems, but all of them.' Escalated beyond the sample to a full audit of all 127 mappings (all classes/properties/relationships/rules/actions) plus, for the first time this session, all 12 competency questions (previously excluded from every manual round as 'requirements, not generated elements').

Text-based rescans (the round-4/5 style: case/no-space label matching, stoplists, synonym clusters) kept finding real gaps but also kept needing new stoplist entries and cluster rules to suppress fresh false positives -- an approach that was clearly still fragile after three rounds of patching it. Replaced it for relationship/action endpoint completeness specifically with a precise, deterministic STRUCTURAL check instead of any text matching: for every relationship, does its own source_iris include at least one already-known IRI for its 'from' class and at least one for its 'to' class (drawn from that class's own classes.<Name> mapping)? Same for every action's 'input' class. This cannot be fooled by phrasing (spaced label vs. compiled name, case, synonyms) because it does not read prose at all -- it only compares structural fields (from/to/input, present in any domain per agent_ontology_spec.md) against already-established citations.

That structural check found 7 relationship gaps and 1 action gap: relationships[7,12,13,14,18,20,33], actions.enableEconomizer. Three of them (relationships[14,18,20]) had rationale text literally reading like '...and the missing cited class IRI should be included' or '...that cited class should be included' -- leftover meta-commentary from round 3's original repair pass that DESCRIBED the fix instead of performing it, undetected until now because nothing checked prose content for this pattern. A fourth item (classes.Thermostat.properties.mode) had the same leftover phrasing but its citation was actually already correct -- cosmetic only.

All 9 real gaps fixed directly (the evidence prose was already correct in every case; only the citation was missing), the 3 leftover-meta-commentary items' rationale text rewritten to be clean and direct, and the cosmetic one cleaned too. Made the fix permanent and general, not another one-off patch: added evaluate.py's new endpoint_citation_gate as a real pipeline layer (2b) and a permanent hard gate -- domain-agnostic, applies to any future domain, not just Brick HVAC -- plus a matching instruction added to compiler-prompt.md and repair-prompt.md so future compiles and repairs are told the requirement up front, not just caught after the fact.

Root-cause code bug found and fixed in reinstate.py, not just Brick HVAC's data: apply_reinstatements() cited only the newly-reinstated class's own IRI on every new relationship it created, never the pre-existing (or same-batch-reinstated) OTHER endpoint's already-known IRI -- exactly the defect class the new gate exists to catch, this time baked into the tool itself rather than a compiler/repair output. Fixed generally with 2 new regression tests.
Full 129-mapping (127 original + 2 added below) independent semantic re-judge: 0 unsupported, 5 contested (disclosed non-blocking borderline splits, same category accepted throughout this domain).

First-ever competency-question audit this session: 3 of 12 (cq5, cq11, cq12) judged not supported by the model as it stood. Investigated each against the real, scoped source material rather than fabricating content to force a pass: cq5 (outside-air vs. return-air CO2 sensing) had real, citable source material (OutsideAirCO2Sensor and ReturnAirCO2Sensor both real Brick classes with real definitions) that simply hadn't been connected to AirHandlingUnit via hasPoint -- fixed by adding two new relationships (relationships[34], relationships[35]), same standard-practice hasPoint grounding already used for the domain's other AHU sensor points. cq11 (chiller/boiler/heat-pump path connectivity) and cq12 (economizer-vs-mechanical-cooling decision logic) were checked against the actual scoped source IR and found to have NO real material to ground the specific claims each CQ asks for (no path/connection-model concept, no outside-air-temperature/enthalpy/mixed-air sensor classes anywhere in this domain's scope) -- fabricating relationships or rules to force these to pass would violate this session's standing no-fabrication rule, so both are left honestly unsupported and documented as genuine scope limits, not defects.
Independent re-judge of the 2 new relationships: 0 unsupported, 0 contested. Re-run cq_support after the fix: cq5 now True; cq11/cq12 remain False, confirmed as real scope limits.
